html:
Unreal material graph automation (UE 5.6.1)

This implementation extends ForgeMCP's existing authenticated native bridge. It does not add editor dependencies to JasperPrism or MajesticForgeRuntime.

Architecture

  • server/main.py registers tools using the official MCP SDK's FastMCP.
  • server/core/materials.py supplies strict Pydantic recipes; arbitrary code, unknown fields, non-finite constants, unsupported expressions and graph cycles are rejected.
  • server/core/connections.py retains loopback connections, session-token [redacted] request correlation, bounded payloads and explicit command allowlists. Material apply uses the existing 60-second timeout; a timeout is an uncertain outcome and must never be blindly retried.
  • MajesticForgeModule.cpp dispatches authenticated requests from its game-thread ticker. ForgeMaterials.cpp independently validates native arguments, mounted package paths, asset identity, pin existence, occupied inputs and graph cycles.
  • Existing Blueprint, actor, GAS, registry, mesh import, transfer, recovery and level-save operations remain registered.
  • MajesticForge is already an Editor module. It now privately depends on MaterialEditor. Unity compilation is disabled for this module because its independent handler translation units contain helper names that collide in a unity translation unit. This is independent of adaptive-unity working sets.

Tool contract

MCP tool Native command Behavior
unreal_inspect_material_graph material_graph_info Inspect the exact material, loading if needed; no edits/compile/save
unreal_preview_material material_preview Review new material creation; refuse existing destinations
unreal_apply_material material_apply Apply creation and validate shaders; remain unsaved
unreal_preview_material_edits material_edit_preview Review additive edits or an isolated compile/save action
unreal_apply_material_edits material_edit_apply Apply the exact reviewed action once
unreal_preview_material_compile material_edit_preview Review compilation only
unreal_compile_material material_edit_apply Explicit apply of a compile preview only
unreal_preview_material_save material_edit_preview Review save after unchanged shader validation
unreal_save_material material_edit_apply Explicit apply of a save preview only

Apply requires an explicit session, the preview ID, and confirmation equal to that ID. Previews expire after 600 seconds, are capped at 32 per session, bind to asset state and operation kind, and are consumed once. Failed/uncertain applies must be inspected before any further mutation.

Compilation and saving both require preview/apply. A compile/save tool cannot consume a preview for a different action. Generic edit apply can consume any reviewed edit/compile/save preview, as its description states.

Supported scope

Destinations are exact package paths under mounted /Game/ or /JasperPrism/. Object paths, redirects, traversal, arbitrary filesystem destinations and other plugin mounts are rejected. /JasperPrism/Materials/M_JasperPrism_PP can be inspected and is protected by default. A narrowly scoped, explicit development_authorization permits only completion of its original three-node contrast graph or compilation of that exact completed four-node graph.

Authorization is an object inside the recipe with asset_path equal to the exact case-sensitive /JasperPrism/Materials/M_JasperPrism_PP, permission equal to I authorize completing the existing JasperPrism contrast graph, and expected_state_id copied from the latest inspection. No ambient authorization, wildcard, global bypass, or authorization for other assets exists. Consent is a caller assertion through the existing authenticated bridge, not independent verification of human identity. Preview/apply confirmation is still required.

Use unreal_preview_material_edits with that object and the exact recipe: one Add alias contrast_add, only parameter const_b=0.5, one connection from the inspected Multiply GUID/output zero to Add.A, and one from Add/output zero to EmissiveColor. No updates, extra expressions, occupied rewiring, or deletions are permitted. Native validation verifies the current three-node input chain, constants, unconnected output, correct domain/location, exact asset identity, and clean baseline before preview and apply. State/fingerprint drift requires a new inspection and preview. Apply retains the authorization in its one-use preview and verifies the completed graph before shader validation.

Authorized compile uses the same generic edit-preview tool with action=compile, no graph changes, fresh state ID, and the same authorization. Only the exact completed four-node graph is accepted. The dedicated compile wrapper remains protected because it supplies no development authorization.

Before an authorized apply, the native bridge copies the exact original disk .uasset into a unique project Saved/MaterialRecovery file and verifies its bytes. Split .uexp/.ubulk packages are unsupported and stop before mutation. The graph journal/in-memory rollback remain in place. This authorization does not permit creation, replacement, or saving an existing asset. Existing-material save requires a separately designed authorization; the normal new-asset save gate is unchanged. Material development must not be applied until its installed plugin and MCP schema have been refreshed and the mechanism has passed testing.

Creation supports Post Process (MD_PostProcess) with Scene Color After Tonemapping (BL_SceneColorAfterTonemapping). Editing preserves these settings and requires them to match. Eight expression types are allowlisted:

  • SceneTexture: scene_texture_id=PostProcessInput0, optional filtered boolean
  • Subtract, Multiply, Add: const_a, const_b
  • Constant: numeric value
  • Constant3Vector: three-component value
  • ScalarParameter: explicit unique parameter_name, numeric default_value
  • VectorParameter: explicit unique parameter_name, RGBA default_value

Creation nodes use recipe-local id aliases and bounded integer x/y positions. Apply returns native expression GUIDs. Updates use those inspected node_id GUIDs, a matching allowlisted type, and a typed parameter dictionary. Existing parameter renaming is excluded because of its effect on material instances.

Connections use from_node, from_output, to_node, to_input. A blank output selects native output zero. SceneTexture's Color alias explicitly selects output zero; channel names are resolved against native output masks. Existing occupied input connections cannot be replaced. Property connections support an unoccupied EmissiveColor only. Changes are checked for graph cycles before apply.

Inspection reports every top-level expression, comment, native input/output, connection output index/mask, property input and editable value within a bound of 256 nodes/comments and bounded response size. Oversized graphs are rejected without truncation. Nested material functions and instances are not expanded.

Native APIs and validation

The Editor module uses UMaterialEditingLibrary::CreateMaterialExpression, ConnectMaterialExpressions, ConnectMaterialProperty and RecompileMaterial. UE 5.6.1's recompile API returns void; this implementation then obtains the active editor material resource at an explicitly captured quality level. UE 5.6.1's PostEditChange uses EMaterialShaderPrecompileMode::None; merely calling FinishCompilation does not submit an unused material's deferred jobs. The validator polls IsCompilationFinished for asynchronous cache readiness, submits the target resource's deferred jobs using SubmitCompileJobs_GameThread, and pumps FShaderCompilingManager::ProcessAsyncResults on the game thread. It reports every GetCompileErrors() message and requires no pending cache/jobs, a complete shader map with shaders, and a full current material shader-map ID and platform match. An empty compiler-error array is never proof of success.

UE 5.6.1 sets whole-map finalization/success flags in ProcessCompiledShaderMaps only when full material-map DDC is enabled or the material is required-complete (default/special engine materials). In lazy per-job-cache mode, an ordinary material's complete rendering clone may legitimately retain both flags false. Waiting longer does not make those flags an unconditional completion contract. The validator reads IsMaterialMapDDCEnabled and IsRequiredComplete rather than changing either engine policy. It subscribes to UMaterial::OnMaterialCompilationFinished before recompile, captures the exact current map only after engine result propagation with finished work, completeness and no resource errors, and removes the listener when validation ends.

Outside lazy mode, finalized/successful flags remain required. In lazy mode with unset flags, a positive completion notification pinned to the exact current map is also required. Completeness alone, an empty error list, a stale map/notification, pending work, and an explicit finalized failure cannot satisfy validation. Missing finalization evidence remains pending until the wait budget expires. Successful notification evidence is retained alongside the validated graph and rechecked against the same map before saving; edits/failure/save/reset invalidate it. The save gate uses the same checks. Diagnostics retain the raw flags and add cache mode, required-complete policy, map identity and completion evidence. Success with lazy-mode evidence reports compile_reason=validated_lazy_shader_job_result. This validates the active editor RHI feature level/material quality, not all cooking targets or visual appearance.

compile_state distinguishes pending, succeeded, failed, unavailable, and timed_out. The synchronous apply returns after success, failure, unavailability, or expiration of its 45-second wait budget; observed intermediate states are included in compile_states_observed. Pending work at expiration is a validation failure and retains the existing rollback policy. compile_reason and compile_diagnostics identify missing resources/maps, skipped compilation, feature/quality levels (including the actual resource quality fallback), pending cache/jobs, map finalization/completeness, shader count, and errors. The budget is checked between engine calls, not a hard interruption of synchronous Unreal APIs. Recompile/cache/result processing can exceed it and the editor game thread is occupied during the wait. This is not an asynchronous MCP operation endpoint. When restoring an existing graph after failure, shader recovery has a separate 5-second wait budget and is reported as rollback_shader_validation. Graph restoration is checked independently; state=rolled_back does not assert that the restored graph has finished shader compilation.

The engine-independent native decision-table test is tests/native/test_material_validation_state.cpp; compile/run it with a C++17 compiler. Python tests exercise MCP preview/apply and authorization independently. Neither test suite proves shader acceptance inside the running Unreal Editor.

Native changes use FScopedTransaction and Modify(). A graph-metadata recovery journal under the project's Saved/MajesticForge/MaterialRecovery is written before graph mutations; it is not a full binary backup. In-memory recovery restores modified values/connections and removes only newly added nodes after failure. State reports completed, rolled_back or partial; transport success does not establish operation success. Failed creation is unregistered and moved to transient storage; a retained empty package may require editor restart before reusing that exact destination.

Saving uses UPackage::SavePackage on the exact package only. It supports only new unsaved materials created by this bridge session, requires an unchanged successful compile fingerprint, rechecks shader status, and refuses existing asset files. Save success requires state=saved and saved=true; a save failure requires inspection of the reported file before retrying. Saved-asset editing is in-memory only in this version. Session restart discards previews and new asset ownership/validation state, so finish an authorized creation/save sequence within one bridge session.

Unsupported in the material-graph tool: arbitrary expression classes/Custom HLSL, material functions, nested graphs, texture binding, expression deletion, rewiring occupied pins, other domains/blend locations/properties, parameter renaming, cross-session preview replay, and all-platform shader checks. Loaded constant material instances now have a separate typed MCP surface documented below; it does not extend the parent graph-expression allowlist.

Material instances

The additional unreal_inspect_material_instance, unreal_preview_material_instance, unreal_apply_material_instance, unreal_preview_material_instance_save and unreal_save_material_instance tools inspect, create, update and save UMaterialInstanceConstant assets. Native inspection returns inherited global scalar, vector RGBA and texture parameters with values and per-instance override flags. Preview validates parameter names and types against the parent, binds the current parameter state, and rejects a stale apply or an existing destination. Parent materials and source graphs remain unchanged.

Create requires an already loaded parent and a new /Game/... or /JasperPrism/... package path. Update requires an already loaded constant material instance. Supported updates are scalar values, four-component linear RGBA values and exact already loaded texture object paths; null sets an explicit empty texture override. Each operation accepts at most 64 changes. Texture loading, recursive package loading and caller-selected filesystem paths are not exposed. Applying creates or updates the in-memory asset; persistence is a separate explicit save preview/apply. New instances must still have no disk package. Existing instances can be saved only after a ForgeMCP-reviewed update in the same bridge session, and only if the package was clean before that update. The save preview binds the in-memory state and current disk-file fingerprint. Save apply first creates and verifies a unique backup under the project's Saved/ForgeMCP/Backups/MaterialInstances directory. The backup is retained after success. If Unreal reports a save failure, the bridge attempts to restore the original disk bytes from the verified backup and reports the disk and in-memory outcome separately; inspect before retrying.

Static switches, component masks, double vectors, texture collections, runtime virtual textures, sparse volume textures and font parameters are reported as unsupported by this increment. Static switches change shader permutations and need a distinct reviewed compile/save lifecycle. The source compiled and linked into the UE 5.6.1 plugin and the package loaded in a disposable project. Actual material-instance parameter editing, backup restoration and save/reopen behavior remain unverified; see Documentation/Development_Status.md.

JasperPrism acceptance checkpoint

The open editor must load a rebuilt native plugin, and the connected MCP client must rediscover the updated Python server. Source tests/build are separate from live material acceptance. Do not forcibly close Unreal or use hot reload to claim the new bridge is installed.

  1. Save any wanted open work and close JasperPrismDev normally.

  2. Build its editor target from PowerShell:

    & '[local path]' JasperPrismDevEditor Win64 Development '-Project=[local path]' -WaitMutex -NoHotReloadFromIDE -NoLiveCoding

  3. After a successful build, reopen JasperPrismDev.uproject, enable/connect ForgeMCP normally, and reconnect the ForgeMCP MCP client to refresh its tools. Use forge_list_sessions to obtain the new session ID; do not assume the old PID.

  4. Continue live acceptance through the discovered tools, or run the prepared script with the new session ID:

    & '[local path]' '[local path]' --session-id unreal-NEWPID

The script refuses an existing test destination. It checks project identity, preview non-mutation, native expression types/connections, constants, explicit compile/edit/save operations, original graph identity, and existing content hashes. It temporarily tests contrast 1.09 and restores 1.08 before save. It persists checkpoints to Saved/MaterialAutomation/live-verification.json and stops on an unexpected result. Do not rerun it blindly after any uncertain or partial result; inspect the target and retained report first.

The authorized test asset is /JasperPrism/Materials/M_ForgeMCP_Test. Its four-node graph is SceneTexture(PostProcessInput0).Color -> Subtract(A, ConstB=0.5) -> Multiply(A, ConstB=1.08) -> Add(A, ConstB=0.5) -> EmissiveColor, using BL_SceneColorAfterTonemapping. No actor, volume, level or original material is assigned or saved by the script.

Exact test-material creation authorization

The new-material preview tool accepts a separate creation_authorization object only for /JasperPrism/Materials/M_ForgeMCP_Test. It must contain that exact asset_path, the exact permission statement I authorize creating the ForgeMCP test material at the exact target path, and expected_state: "absent". The native editor rechecks that the exact package path is absent on preview and again on apply, and rejects case aliases, existing packages, the existing-material authorization, and this creation authorization on edit/compile/save requests. The original M_JasperPrism_PP authorization remains separate and unchanged. All typed-node, graph, transaction, rollback, shader validation and save gates continue to apply. The authorization does not create or save the asset by itself; preview and apply remain separate operations.
